PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: character-moses-freed-prophet-appearance
Workflow profile: 4X3 (4:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Character guard: the row alone defines identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, hair, scars, costume, wounds, pose, and carried objects. Never turn a non-Jesus character into a Jesus lookalike.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain; explicitly requested production-sheet spacing/readability only.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
MOSES - FREED PROPHET — APPEARANCE: FOUR-VIEW IDENTITY, ANATOMY, COSTUME, AND CONTINUITY REFERENCE.

Create a four-view cinematic character ingredients sheet showing the same person in frontal three-quarter portrait, full-body, side profile, and rear-head/costume view. Lock facial identity, age, ethnicity, hairline, complete crown and rear hair, costume construction, body proportions, hands, scars, wounds, and carried props across every panel. One face exists only on the front of the head. Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Moses the Freed Prophet at the exact moment of liberation inside Hell's Inner Chamber: an elderly Levantine Hebrew man approximately five feet ten inches tall, lean ascetic build with long-lived wiry strength rather than bulk, roughly seventy to eighty years in weathered appearance yet still upright and purposeful. Long pure white hair falls past the shoulders in thick silver-white waves, fully covering the crown and rear of the head with no bald patch; the hairline is high and noble but complete, strands slightly matted at the temples with fine pale dust of long captivity yet still orderly, as if habit of care never left him. A full long white beard descends to mid-chest, dense and well-shaped despite imprisonment, framing a gaunt dignified face of deep olive-brown Mediterranean skin sun-etched and then further lined by ages of waiting. Forehead broad and creased with vertical thought-lines; cheekbones high and spare; nose strong and slightly arched; mouth firm, thin-lipped, capable of command yet now soft with gratitude. Eyes are dark brown, sharp and brilliantly intelligent, still marked by the memory of divine encounter on Sinai—a quiet fire of recognition rather than rage—reflecting warm amber and gold as chains fall away. No scars of battle; only the gentle wear of wilderness years, faint freckling of age spots on temples and backs of hands, and the newly brightened expression of a man who has just been freed by the Redeemer he foreshadowed.

Costume is simple natural-fiber shepherd garments in earth tones: a long rough-spun undyed linen and coarse wool tunic in dusty oatmeal, warm sand, and muted clay-brown, ankle-length, slightly oversized through the chest from lean frame, hem frayed and thinned to translucency at the lower edge. A second wrap or cloak of heavier natural wool in deeper umber-brown hangs from the shoulders, unevenly faded, with small tears near the hem and a soft greying of fiber from soot and time. A plain braided leather cord or narrow hide belt cinches the waist; no metal ornaments, no jewelry, no embroidery of kings—only the dignity of a shepherd-prophet. Bare forearms show lean muscle and pronounced tendons; hands are large, work-worn, knuckles slightly enlarged, fingernails short and clean enough for a man of law, palms showing old calluses from staff and desert labor. Feet in simple worn leather sandals with thin straps, dusted pale ash, toes long and strong. Continuity lock with wardrobe asset ward-moses: natural-fiber shepherd garments, worn but maintaining dignity, never royal cloth, never animal skins (those belong to Elijah and John).

Primary carried prop continuity: Moses' ancient wooden staff held in the right hand as symbol of divine authority and deliverance. The staff is roughly six feet of weathered hardwood—olive or desert acacia grain suggested—dark honey-brown wood polished smooth where palms have gripped for generations, slight bow from age, bark long gone, faint natural spiral grain and subtle darker mineral-like markings along the shaft as if scorched once by holy fire, never a modern stick or carved tourist prop. Left hand is free in this liberated beat: open, reaching slightly toward the invading golden light, fingers spread in recognition and humble acceptance rather than grasp. Body language is upright, shoulders squared but not martial; weight evenly on both feet after chains release; chin lifted toward the source of light with profound recognition and gratitude, authority tempered by humility.

Four-view cinematic character ingredients sheet of this identical person locked across all panels:
(1) Frontal three-quarter portrait from mid-chest up: face fully readable, white beard and hair volume, eyes catching divine gold rim light, staff head or upper shaft partially visible at frame edge, expression of liberation and spiritual depth, skin pores and age texture photoreal.
(2) Full-body standing view: entire figure including sandals and full staff length, tunic drape and cloak fall, lean proportions, belt knot, free hand toward light, slight three-quarter turn so face remains clear.
(3) Strict side profile left or right: silhouette of aquiline nose, flowing white beard line, hair crown height, ear placement, staff vertical line parallel to body, shepherd garment layers in profile.
(4) Rear-head and costume view: complete white hair covering rear scalp and nape, no second face, cloak and tunic back construction, belt rear, staff held visible along right side from behind, shoulder slope and spine posture of an elderly but unbroken prophet.

Environment context for lighting and atmosphere only (not a full location plate): Hell's Inner Chamber at the liberation beat after chains break—vast black-stone architecture still partially present, blue torch remnants dying at the edges while ethereal gold and warm amber divine radiance floods from Jesus' presence and the sword of light. Soft volumetric god rays cut through residual smoke and ash; fine pale dust and freed-chain particulate hang in the air. Color grade for this character beat: warm amber and soft gold key on skin and white hair against cool residual blue-black shadow falloff, deep crimson ambient bounce minimal, transitioning hell palette toward perfume-warm amber of transformation. Subsurface scattering in ears and thin beard edges; fabric translucency at worn tunic hems; wood grain of staff readable under side light.

Lighting design: soft but directional golden key from upper front-three-quarter (divine intrusion ~5500–6500K mixed with warm amber ~3500K fill), cool blue-violet edge fill from distant dying hell torches (~2000–4000K) for separation only, gentle rim along white hair and beard fibers, no harsh modern studio softboxes, physically coherent shadows. Camera language for production reference panels: clean orthographic-adjacent multi-view layout, approximately 50–85mm portrait equivalent feel for face panels and 35–50mm for full body, shallow-to-medium depth of field keeping eyes and staff grip sharp, 2.39:1 sensibility within each panel framing without letterbox graphics. Photoreal live-action biblical epic production reference quality equal to a major studio character sheet—exact anatomy, clean five-fingered hands, consistent scale, no modern objects, no logos, no text, no watermarks, no borders, no captions, no UI. One face exists only on the front of the head in every panel; rear view shows only hair and costume. Lock facial identity, age, ethnicity, hairline, complete crown and rear hair, costume construction, body proportions, hands, and staff across every panel. Sacred reverent tone, not fantasy excess, not gore, not cartoon.
